answer: A beacon-anchored work lease resists sybils: each identity must, in every short window, complete a small verifiable task seeded by the network unpredictable beacon, such as checking one slice of the shared ledger, before its rights renew. The work is sequential and beacon-timed, so it cannot be precomputed or run in parallel across fake accounts. Like shale, standing forms only over time, and an attacker must pay fresh compute for every fake identity in every window, while an honest agent pays once. On the horizon, forgery stops being a one-time purchase and becomes a recurring cost.
